item.title: KL Tower: Reopening concessions fosters competition, says ministry
item.description:
The Communications Ministry says the government has opened proposals to run the iconic Kuala Lumpur Tower in order to foster competition.

In a list of “frequently asked questions” issued last night, it said the government has the discretion to do so even if the existing concessionaire has held the concession for a long time.

item.title: KL Tower management grateful 'eviction' averted
item.description:
Hydroshoppe Sdn Bhd, which owns Kuala Lumpur Tower concessionaire Menara Kuala Lumpur Sdn Bhd (MKLSB), has expressed gratitude for not being evicted.

item.title: Action on KL Tower will be in accordance with law, says ministry
item.description:
The Communications Ministry has affirmed that any action regarding Kuala Lumpur Tower will be done in accordance with the law, amid a legal dispute over its concession agreement.

“As such, the ministry urges all parties to give space for the legal process to proceed smoothly.

item.title: KL Tower: Hydroshoppe calls late-night presser over eviction fears
item.description:
The former operator of Kuala Lumpur Tower has called for a late-night press conference tonight over fears that they could be evicted at the stroke of midnight.

This came after a letter was circulated online purporting that the Communications Ministry has affirmed LSH Service Master Sdn Bhd (LSHSM) will take over KL Tower’s management and operations as the new concession holder effective tomorrow.

item.title: Prasarana submits fatal LRT accident report to ministry, Apad
item.description:
The report on the fatal incident involving a visually impaired man who was run over by a train after falling onto the Titiwangsa LRT tracks on Feb 22 has been submitted to the Transport Ministry and the Land Public Transport Agency (Apad).

Prasarana Malaysia Berhad president and group chief executive officer Azharuddin Mat Sah said the report was prepared by a committee established to investigate the tragedy and recommend improvements to prevent similar incidents.
item.author: Bernama

item.title: Army man who attacked female driver freed on bail
item.description:
An armed forced personnel, who had been arrested after he attacked a female driver of a Perodua Axia along Jalan Persiaran Senawang 4 following an accident, was released on police bail yesterday.

Seremban district police chief Hatta Che Din said the case has also been referred to Bukit Aman as the suspect, 35, was a civil servant.
item.author: Bernama

item.title: Environmental group criticises S'gor for skipping Zero Waste Day
item.description:
The Rawang Tolak Incinerator Network (RTI) pressure group criticised the Selangor government for promoting billion-ringgit incinerator projects instead of implementing International Zero Waste Day.

RTI said observing Zero Waste Day would not have been a mere symbolic gesture but would reflect the government’s commitment to resolving waste management issues.

item.title: Nga: Local councils, petty traders must follow law for mutual benefit
item.description:

item.title: Israeli strikes kill 33, including 13 children in Gaza
item.description:
Thirty-three Palestinians, including 13 children, have been killed and several others injured since early Sunday in Israeli airstrikes across several areas in the Gaza Strip on the first day of Aidilfitri, Anadolu Ajansi reported.

Witnesses and medics told Anadolu that Israeli airstrikes targeted homes, a tent shelter, and civilian vehicles in Gaza City, Jabalia in the north, and Khan Younis in the south.
item.author: Bernama

item.title: Cops identify siblings, mother as victims in fatal Karak highway crash
item.description:
Police have identified three victims who were killed in a five-vehicle collision at KM50.8 of the Kuala Lumpur-Karak-Kuala Lumpur (KLK) Expressway yesterday.

Bentong police chief Zaiham Mohd Kahar said that the victims were identified as the driver of a Honda Accord, Wong Kean Yeap, 29, along with the passengers - his sister, Wong Hwee Moon, 34, and their mother, Lee Lai Cheng, 61...

item.description:

item.title: 'Let Syawal symbolise unity, gratitude to the divine'
item.description:
The celebration of Hari Raya Aidilfitri is not only a sign of victory for Muslims who have fasted for a month but also a symbol of harmony among a multi-ethnic society and an opportunity to express gratitude to the Almighty, according to a reminder from the Malay rulers.

In Selangor, Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah and his consort Norashikin hoped that Muslims in Malaysia would celebrate Aidilfitri in a lively, harmonious and united atmosphere.

item.title: Selamat Hari Raya from Malaysiakini
item.description:
Selamat Hari Raya from the Malaysiakini team to all our Muslim friends.

We wish all our readers a safe trip and joyous Raya festivities with your loved ones.

The Malaysiakini team will be operating on a skeleton staff for the festive season, but we will be back at full strength on April 2 to bring our readers more news and views that matter.
item.author: Malaysiakini Team

item.title: Cops probe 3 police reports on balloon vendor altercation
item.description:
Police are investigating three reports related to an altercation between a street vendor and Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) enforcers, including allegations of obstruction, threats, and causing grievous injury.

In the meantime, Kuala Lumpur deputy police chief Azry Akmar Ayob urged members of the public not to speculate on the case to avoid interfering with investigations.

Seremban district police chief Mohamad Hatta Che Din said the man, 35, was arrested at the Seremban district police headquarters this afternoon to facilitate investigations under Sections 323 and 427 of the Penal Code.

item.title: Questioning Musa's birthday celebration is check-and-balance: Warisan
item.description:
Warisan has defended its questioning of the arrangements for official celebrations of Sabah governor Musa Aman’s birthday after Chief Minister Hajiji Noor accused the party of dragging the palace into politics.

Warisan president Shafie Apdal said these were merely honest questions and were not an attack or insult on the state palace.

item.title: DBKL puts 3 officers on leave over balloon vendor incident
item.description:
The Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) has put three officers on leave after their involvement in an incident on Jalan Tuanku Abdul Rahman two days ago.

The decision was made after a meeting with Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Dr Zaliha Mustafa, Kuala Lumpur mayor Maimunah Mohd Sharif said today.

item.title: Instilling patriotism requires more than badges on uniforms - Lee
item.description:
The government’s initiative requiring students to wear the Jalur Gemilang badge on their school uniforms from April 21 serves as a symbolic reminder of national identity and unity, said National Unity Advisory Council member Lee Lam Thye.

While welcoming the initiative, Lee, however, emphasised that true loyalty to the nation must go beyond symbols and be nurtured through education, engagement, and real-life experiences.
item.author: Bernama

item.title: Sabah tops Sara aid list with close to 500k recipients
item.description:
Sabah has the highest number of Rahmah Necessities Aid (Sara) recipients, said Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Armizan Mohd Ali.

Armizan said Sabahans accounted for nearly 500,000 recipients, who received a total of more than RM492 million.
